bull_bear.body:
- Production has not resumed — The MD&A names 'above all failure to resume production' among the factors adversely impacting business prospects and profitability, and the segment commentary says the Company is exploring real estate and textile markets but 'as of now there is no projects in the Company' — so the operating business is effectively dormant and earnings rest on non-operating sources.
- Collapse in readymade-garment export demand — Management states that during 2025-26 exports of readymade garments reduced substantially and export growth was severely affected by several internal and external developments, and that the Company 'is seized of all such factors having adverse effect on its exports'.
- Highly competitive and fragmented knitwear industry with persistent pricing pressure — The MD&A describes the knitwear sector as highly competitive and fragmented and says textile companies are always experiencing pricing pressures, lately due to stiff international competition — limiting realisations and any pricing power.
- Technology and fashion obsolescence, with no upgradation spend — Changing technology and fashion, and lack of modern technology, are flagged as significant threats, yet capital expenditure on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment during the year was Nil — so the stated mitigation was not funded.
- Labour-law rigidity — 'Archaic personnel laws' are listed by management among the areas of significant threat to the business.
- Unproven diversification into real estate — The Company says it endeavours into real estate to raise profit but confirms it entered into no real-estate contracts during the year under review and has no projects — an intention, not an operating second leg.
- Change of management and control — A Share Purchase and Transfer of Control Agreement dated May 20, 2025 led to a completed open offer, a wholesale board turnover in December 2025 and a new management team — a discontinuity in strategy, execution track record and governance continuity.
- Compliance lapse flagged by the Secretarial Auditor, and a capital commitment with no named project — The secretarial audit records delay in appointment of the Chief Financial Officer within three months of the vacancy as required by Regulation 26A(2) of SEBI LODR, alongside a secretarial-auditor change mid-year following the resignation of the previous firm; separately, the accounts carry open capital commitments with no project or timeline disclosed. Note also that the Board's Report asserts the Company 'has not identified any element of risk which may threaten its existence or such risks are very minimal' and the MD&A 'Risks & Concerns' section contains only mitigation boilerplate — it enumerates no risks — so the risks above are drawn from the MD&A's industry and opportunities/threats commentary and the audit reports rather than from a risk disclosure.

outlook.body:
- Explore real estate alongside textiles to lift Company profit — management states it 'endeavours into real estate to upward the profit of the Company', while disclosing that no real-estate contracts were entered into during the year and that as of now there are no projects in the Company.
- Continue to explore options to strengthen the capital base and balance sheet to augment long-term resources for business activities, future growth opportunities and general corporate purposes (stated under Future Prospects and Outlook).
- Thrust on product excellence, judicious risk management, constant monitoring of risk factors and greater market penetration as the stated guides to business strategy.
- Strict monitoring of costs and overheads, wherever feasible, to make the product more price-competitive.
- Constantly update plant and equipment to produce best-quality products — though the MD&A records that capital expenditure of Nil was incurred during the year on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no expansion project, no capacity addition and no commissioning timeline. The MD&A states that capital expenditure of Nil was incurred during the year on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment, that the Company is exploring markets in real estate and textiles but 'as of now there is no projects in the Company', and that no real-estate contracts were entered into during the year. The Directors' Report adds that no manufacturing activity or technology absorption was undertaken during the year, that capital investment on energy-conservation equipment was Nil and that R&D expenditure was Nil. The only quantified capital item is a capital-commitments note: estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account (net of advances) of 1,705.96 lakhs as at March 31, 2026 against Nil a year earlier, with no project named and no timeline given — so the underlying commitment cannot be identified from this text. The other corporate development of the year was the completed open offer and transfer of management control to the new acquirers, not a capacity event.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management says opportunities in the textile industry and increasing growth in export of knitted garments 'augur well for this vital segment', and cites a perceptible shift in outlook towards diversified and high value-added products (management claim).
- Against that, the MD&A states that during 2025-26 exports of readymade garments reduced substantially and export growth was severely affected, attributing it to stiff global competition, changing technology and fashion, and 'above all failure to resume production', which adversely impact business prospects and profitability.
- Persistent pricing pressure from stiff international competition, plus lack of modern technology and archaic personnel laws, are flagged as significant threats; the Company says it 'is seized of all such factors having adverse effect on its exports'.
- Macro framing cited by management: global growth projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, with India's GDP growth projected at 6.4% in 2026 and 6.6% in 2027 per the IMF and the United Nations; rising crude prices from Middle East tensions may raise import costs and pressure the rupee.
- The knitwear sector is described as highly competitive and fragmented.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Readymade garment / knitted garment exports (the Company states export growth was severely affected and that it is seized of factors adversely affecting its exports)
- Real estate (stated exploratory interest only; no projects and no contracts entered during the year)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management says opportunities in the textile industry and increasing growth in export of knitted garments 'augur well for this vital segment', and cites a perceptible shift in outlook towards diversified and high value-added products (management claim).
- Against that, the MD&A states that during 2025-26 exports of readymade garments reduced substantially and export growth was severely affected, attributing it to stiff global competition, changing technology and fashion, and 'above all failure to resume production', which adversely impact business prospects and profitability.
- Persistent pricing pressure from stiff international competition, plus lack of modern technology and archaic personnel laws, are flagged as significant threats; the Company says it 'is seized of all such factors having adverse effect on its exports'.
- Macro framing cited by management: global growth projected to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, with India's GDP growth projected at 6.4% in 2026 and 6.6% in 2027 per the IMF and the United Nations; rising crude prices from Middle East tensions may raise import costs and pressure the rupee.
- The knitwear sector is described as highly competitive and fragmented.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Explore real estate alongside textiles to lift Company profit — management states it 'endeavours into real estate to upward the profit of the Company', while disclosing that no real-estate contracts were entered into during the year and that as of now there are no projects in the Company.
- Continue to explore options to strengthen the capital base and balance sheet to augment long-term resources for business activities, future growth opportunities and general corporate purposes (stated under Future Prospects and Outlook).
- Thrust on product excellence, judicious risk management, constant monitoring of risk factors and greater market penetration as the stated guides to business strategy.
- Strict monitoring of costs and overheads, wherever feasible, to make the product more price-competitive.
- Constantly update plant and equipment to produce best-quality products — though the MD&A records that capital expenditure of Nil was incurred during the year on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no expansion project, no capacity addition and no commissioning timeline. The MD&A states that capital expenditure of Nil was incurred during the year on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment, that the Company is exploring markets in real estate and textiles but 'as of now there is no projects in the Company', and that no real-estate contracts were entered into during the year. The Directors' Report adds that no manufacturing activity or technology absorption was undertaken during the year, that capital investment on energy-conservation equipment was Nil and that R&D expenditure was Nil. The only quantified capital item is a capital-commitments note: estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account (net of advances) of 1,705.96 lakhs as at March 31, 2026 against Nil a year earlier, with no project named and no timeline given — so the underlying commitment cannot be identified from this text. The other corporate development of the year was the completed open offer and transfer of management control to the new acquirers, not a capacity event.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Production has not resumed — The MD&A names 'above all failure to resume production' among the factors adversely impacting business prospects and profitability, and the segment commentary says the Company is exploring real estate and textile markets but 'as of now there is no projects in the Company' — so the operating business is effectively dormant and earnings rest on non-operating sources.
- Collapse in readymade-garment export demand — Management states that during 2025-26 exports of readymade garments reduced substantially and export growth was severely affected by several internal and external developments, and that the Company 'is seized of all such factors having adverse effect on its exports'.
- Highly competitive and fragmented knitwear industry with persistent pricing pressure — The MD&A describes the knitwear sector as highly competitive and fragmented and says textile companies are always experiencing pricing pressures, lately due to stiff international competition — limiting realisations and any pricing power.
- Technology and fashion obsolescence, with no upgradation spend — Changing technology and fashion, and lack of modern technology, are flagged as significant threats, yet capital expenditure on technology upgradation and modernisation of machinery and equipment during the year was Nil — so the stated mitigation was not funded.
- Labour-law rigidity — 'Archaic personnel laws' are listed by management among the areas of significant threat to the business.
- Unproven diversification into real estate — The Company says it endeavours into real estate to raise profit but confirms it entered into no real-estate contracts during the year under review and has no projects — an intention, not an operating second leg.
- Change of management and control — A Share Purchase and Transfer of Control Agreement dated May 20, 2025 led to a completed open offer, a wholesale board turnover in December 2025 and a new management team — a discontinuity in strategy, execution track record and governance continuity.
- Compliance lapse flagged by the Secretarial Auditor, and a capital commitment with no named project — The secretarial audit records delay in appointment of the Chief Financial Officer within three months of the vacancy as required by Regulation 26A(2) of SEBI LODR, alongside a secretarial-auditor change mid-year following the resignation of the previous firm; separately, the accounts carry open capital commitments with no project or timeline disclosed. Note also that the Board's Report asserts the Company 'has not identified any element of risk which may threaten its existence or such risks are very minimal' and the MD&A 'Risks & Concerns' section contains only mitigation boilerplate — it enumerates no risks — so the risks above are drawn from the MD&A's industry and opportunities/threats commentary and the audit reports rather than from a risk disclosure.

hero.oneLiner: Addi Industries Limited is a Delhi-headquartered knitwear/textile company that has not resumed production and is exploring real estate alongside textiles, having passed to new promoters via a 74.27% stake sale and open offer completed in FY 2025-26.
